As he left Milanello earlier this evening, Gerry Cardinale stopped to share a few words on the game against Frosinone, the January mercato, Markus Krösche and more.

Recent findings suggest that cardinale arrived in Milan a few days ago and had a summit with the management at Casa Milan yesterday. In other words, he’s not wasting any time, making every second of his trip to the city count.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Today, he was at Milanello to watch the team’s training session and Amorim’s press conference, and tomorrow he will be at the game against Frosinone.

It has been revealed that the owner left the training ground shortly after 4 pm today, but before driving away, he rolled down the window and spoke to the journalists present. In addition to the game, he also spoke about the upcoming mercato and what Milan intend to do.

According to recent reports, “I’m ready for tomorrow. We had a great couple of days, including a session at Casa Milan yesterday on the mercato, as well as the rest of our aims for the season going into the summer. I’d say that the mood is really upbeat here, it was a great session today and the team is really coming together.

“I spoke to a bunch of the players, they are all feeling really positive, and they understand as Ruben mentioned how key tomorrow’s game is. Hopefully, we come out strong, get the win and keep going.”.

It has been revealed that “Yeah I’m ready. We are doing a lot of work. It’s complicated and the January transfer window is always tricky. So you have to be prepared, you have to be opportunistic. The one thing I can promise is that we won’t make any decision that we don’t feel great about.

“We will spend money, but we will spend money smart and with a view to being consistent with the project, in close coordination with Ruben and everyone here at Milanello.”.

According to recent reports, “With Markus Krösche. I know you guys have been very focused on Markus, but when we’re ready to make an announcement, I will come back to you guys on it.”.

Sources indicate that “Look, that name also keeps getting mentioned. This project is more than just one player, but he’s one of the best players, if not the best player, in his position. So tremendous amount of respect from me and we will see what’s possible.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Look, I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s just fantastic and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We are in discussions and I hope that we will have a good result. But if it were up to me, he would be a franchise player.”.

It has been revealed that clearly, there’s a lot happening right now and Milan are hoping that the addition of Krösche to the management will help them get even better control. It would certainly raise the enthusiasm if they were to have a good mercato and secure a renewal for Adrien Rabiot.

According to recent reports, cardinale: “Ho parlato con i giocatori sono molto concentrati. Endrick e’ uno dei migliori giocatori al mondo, ci proveremo, vediamo se sarà una possibilità di mercato. Rabiot? E’ un giocatore fantastico vogliamo che sia anche per il futuro” https://t.co/bf9mcZulbG.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham have slipped down to 12th place in the Championship table following their 1-0 loss away at Portsmouth on Tuesday night. WHUFC are now three points off the top eight behind Swansea City.

Recent findings suggest that the Hammers turned to Scott Parker as their head coach earlier this month after their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. However, the ex-Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley man has struggled to make an impact so far and is yet to win in his first four games at the helm.

Brazil, who played for the likes of Ipswich Town, Tottenham Hotspur and QPR during his playing days, has delivered his verdict on the London outfit on talkSPORT: “It’s only four games (for Parker). I’m sure he can turn that around but defensively they are giving so many easy goals away. They’ve got to stop that.”.

Sources indicate that he added: “Listen, I still think they’ll be hovering top six (eight). I was hoping that they’d have a great start. I like West Ham but it hasn’t to be.”.

West Ham are back in action this weekend as they aim to return to winning ways. They take on high flying Stoke City at the London Stadium.

Sources indicate that west Ham haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last six matches. As Brazil has alluded to, WHUFC have been leaking too many goals.

Industry observers note that the Hammers need to tighten up their defensive department if they are to turn their fortunes around over the coming weeks. They will get the chance to bring in some new faces when the January transfer window opens up for business.

Recent findings suggest that parker will be eager to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad this winter. He knows what it takes to get out of the second tier having guided Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley up in the past.

Sources indicate that he is under pressure already at West Ham though, despite only being four games into his spell. If they lose again against Stoke City on Saturday, the heat will be further intensified.

West Ham are still the top scorers in the division. WHUFC have scored 38 goals in their 17 fixtures.

In a recent development, the Hammers are always a threat going forward and if they can bolster their backline, there is no reason why they can’t rise back up the league. They managed to keep hold of Jarrod Bowen in the summer and he has found the net on nine occasions this term.

In a recent development, parker will be disappointed with his start as manager but the players are still getting used to his style. He won’t get patience from the supporters though and needs wins fast.

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

Mauricio Pochettino was immediately up against it in his first few days at this slow-motion car crash of a club - Man United's 4-0 loss at Liverpool highlighted how much he has to do: OLIVER HOLT

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1628 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.
  • That was before the football started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026.

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

That was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

Sources indicate that and then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

According to recent reports, so at least Pochettino got to see United set a new record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more rapidly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his substantial coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United.

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars.

Recent findings suggest that and in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

And the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

Industry observers note that so, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

Industry observers note that this is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

It has been revealed that in that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a big ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

It was strange seeing a new United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

In a recent development, it did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game.

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise.

According to recent reports, isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

In a recent development, A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa.

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82.

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46).

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey.

Sources indicate that three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

Industry observers note that united were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

In a recent development, and so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

Sources indicate that there was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

According to recent reports, that feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

According to recent reports, liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

Sources indicate that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant mentioned: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

In a recent development, “They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a major game again on Tuesday so it’s key to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

“We’ve had a great week. A latest manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

It has been revealed that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

Recent findings suggest that “I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

In a recent development, “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

Pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

It has been revealed that scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

According to recent reports, another big chance for Scotland. This time Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie goes close.Slovenia 0-0 Scotland - watch the closing stages on BBC One. pic.twitter.com/xMe5gRNgEr.

Industry observers note that from the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

In a recent development, welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

It has been revealed that another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

McGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

Gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

The second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

McBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

According to recent reports, mcBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

McGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

Recent findings suggest that we are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a fresh system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

HALF TIME: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland.No goals at the break in Ljubljana.#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/6VGFRprBiz.

In a recent development, ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Scotland's best chance of the game so far 😯 Sevilla striker and debutant Robbie Ure strikes the post just before half-time.However, it remains goalless at the break.📺 Watch Slovenia v Scotland on BBC One 🇸🇮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 pic.twitter.com/fm1wH2fOej.

Much better from Scotland! McGinn turns his marker and clips a wonderful pass over to Ure, who has drifted out wide. The ball is then delivered into the box toward McGinn, whose header bounces off McBurnie. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

Robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Recent findings suggest that matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

It’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

Similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

It has been revealed that since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

The hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

It has been revealed that slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is launched forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

It has been revealed that slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A newly introduced-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that debutants Robbie Ure and Stephen Welsh are each poised for their first international cap. Billy Gilmour returns to the starting XI after missing the World Cup through injury and Oli McBurnie will make his first appearance for Scotland since 2021.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most key thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

“I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

Sources indicate that “We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

According to recent reports, scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his fresh role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

Tech Report: Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that reservoirs need to be constructed in ways that help to avoid water shortages as heatwaves increase.
  • According to recent reports, “Prepare for El Niño”, the World Meteorological Organization warned earlier this year.
  • Recent findings suggest that repeated disasters cause immense disruption to people’s lives and livelihoods, and the economic loss and damage can add up to trillions of dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that reservoirs need to be constructed in ways that help to avoid water shortages as heatwaves increase. Credit: Ander Gillenea/AFP via Getty.

According to recent reports, “Prepare for El Niño”, the World Meteorological Organization warned earlier this year. Governments are responding by adjusting agricultural practices and securing water supplies. But climate measures should not begin when a hazardous event approaches, they should be part of a wider strategy of planning for a warmer future.

Recent findings suggest that repeated disasters cause immense disruption to people’s lives and livelihoods, and the economic loss and damage can add up to trillions of dollars. Climate warnings and actions taken in anticipation of disasters can help to reduce the impact on people and economies. But their effectiveness is constrained by existing limitations, such as a community’s access to resources and infrastructure.

Such vulnerabilities must be addressed at their source, when decisions about development and infrastructure are being made, so that climate risks are reduced through better planning rather than through reactive responses to individual events. Decisions about the location and capacity of reservoirs, agricultural drainage systems and the design of cities and transport infrastructure, for instance, cannot be changed easily once they have been made.

In a recent development, much of what is being built now will shape societies for decades. To meet global climate and development objectives by 2030, nearly US$7 trillion of infrastructure investment is needed annually1. Global annual infrastructure spending is projected to increase from $4.4 trillion in 2024 to $6.9 trillion by 20502. But it will be wasted if projects are designed inadequately for the climate conditions that people will face.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

It has been revealed that decisions for development projects are being hampered because climate projections are often not integrated into planning processes. Another challenge is the limited availability of reliable, decision-relevant climate information for the 5–30-year period — an intermediate timescale between seasonal forecasts and long-term climate projections that is particularly relevant for planning major infrastructure such as roads and reservoirs3.

It has been revealed that climate services can provide this information. Scientists can improve climate projections. Development planners can assess projects. But unless these functions are connected within the development process, the system as a whole remains reactive.

Sources indicate that A common operating system would change that. Government ministries that oversee development would determine which planning decisions need to consider climate information. Planning institutions would ensure that climate assessments are undertaken and considered as part of investment approval for climate-sensitive projects. Climate agencies would provide the scientific information, which would improve both planning and science. Here, I outline how such a system would work.

It has been revealed that A central government planning institution should establish a small climate-planning unit within it, not separately. Corresponding units could be set up in state or subnational planning institutions when appropriate. In countries without central planning institutions, the same functions could be assigned to existing government institutions.

Recent findings suggest that the central unit would set common standards, consolidate information needs across sectors and jurisdictions, coordinate with national climate agencies and ensure that climate considerations are incorporated into the planning and appraisal of projects of national significance. Subnational units would apply the framework to local projects and feed emerging requirements back to the central unit.

Sources indicate that responsibilities should be made explicit. Ministries should identify the climate information needed to support various sectors. Planning institutions would coordinate those needs and ensure that such climate information informs investment decisions. Climate agencies would produce the underlying scientific information and ensure its technical accuracy and quality.

This division matters. The proposal is not to make development planners become climate scientists, nor to make climate agencies become development authorities. It is to give them a permanent institutional connection.

The rules governing public investment in development should be changed to follow this principle: funding for a major climate-sensitive project should not be approved without a demonstration that it has been designed for the climate it is expected to face.

Governments should request climate assessments for large, long-lived and climate-sensitive projects before approving funds. Assessments should be provided early enough in the process to influence the location, technology, scale and design of a project. For a new reservoir, for example, the relevant planning unit would identify the climate conditions that the reservoir is likely to face during its operational lifetime, with implications for where and how it is built.

According to recent reports, A climate-planning unit would not decide whether the project should proceed; it would certify that the relevant climate risks have been assessed and that reasonable alternatives have been considered. Its assessment would be considered as part of an investment appraisal alongside economic, technical, social and environmental factors.

To be effective, the system must connect three functions: development demand, climate analysis and investment approval.

Ministries should periodically identify the climate information needed for their forthcoming development decisions. The central planning unit should consolidate these requests and work with climate agencies to determine what information can be provided, what projects require fresh analysis and when investment for climate observations, modelling or scientific capacity is needed.

Kenya’s government is implementing measures to reduce flooding from rivers.Credit: James Wakibia/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty.

Sources indicate that this comprehensive approach would provide climate scientists with clear directives from the development system. It would encourage them to improve climate projections for specific regions, over a 5–30-year typical planning horizon, and for distinct sectors. It would also reduce the need for individual development projects to commission their own climate analyses, which can be patchy and inconsistent.

An analysis of six generations of assessment reports from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change found, for instance, that inconsistent climate projections across many low- and middle-income countries were complicating adaptation and long-term planning efforts4. For example, in some regions, precipitation was projected by one assessment to increase, and by the next to decrease, with successive views bouncing back and forth.

Such disagreements undermine a region’s ability to make long-term investments. They increase the likelihood of costly misallocation of funds, maladaptation to climate risks and infrastructure being developed that is ill-suited to future climate conditions. Dams, cities and transport corridors cannot be easily redesigned or rebuilt once constructed.

According to recent reports, this challenge is compounded by the fact that climate models perform poorly across many climate-vulnerable regions. In South Asia, for example, simulations of temperature and precipitation can differ from observed values by as much as 25% and 100%, respectively5. Such biases limit the reliability of model-based climate information for guiding long-term development decisions.

It has been revealed that that’s why the proposed climate-informed planning units would ensure that climate agencies’ work is guided by clearly articulated development needs and that the information they provide is reliable and fit for development planning. Importantly, they would not be a replacement for other climate services, which can remain focused on providing accurate information for a wide range of sectors6,7. The aim is to bridge a specific gap between climate information and development.

A climate assessment for a development project should not become obsolete as soon as the work is approved. Both central and subnational planning units should regularly monitor whether new climate observations or scientific assessments change the climate risks identified. If they do, an updated assessment should be returned to the planning authority.

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming.

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming.

According to recent reports, the units should evaluate whether the climate information generated by the system is useful. Regular technical reviews would compare climate projections with observations and assess whether the information remains fit for planning purposes. Institutional reviews conducted by climate-planning units could also examine whether big projects have incorporated climate foresight and whether it influenced their designs.

These reviews would create a feedback loop. Development decisions would determine what information is needed, which could be satisfied by climate-science and investment-appraisal processes. Data from implemented projects would then be fed back into the system to update climate information and plans going forwards.

Leeds United, Brentford interested in Leicester City teenager – three European clubs also keen

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City have seen a handful of new starlets find more regular roles in the first team since their drop to League One.
  • Recent findings suggest that among them is 18-year-old winger Bismark Owusu, and according to reporter Pete O’Rourke, a string of clubs are interested in prising him away from the King Power Stadium.
  • Owusu has been a regular in the Foxes’ U18s side for some time and he has stepped up his involvement in the U21s group this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City have seen a handful of new starlets find more regular roles in the first team since their drop to League One. Louis Page, Will Alves and Sammy Braybrooke are all mainstays under Russell Martin, and there’s a crop of impressive prospects impressing in the LCFC youth ranks as well.

Recent findings suggest that among them is 18-year-old winger Bismark Owusu, and according to reporter Pete O’Rourke, a string of clubs are interested in prising him away from the King Power Stadium. Premier League pair Leeds United and Brentford are remarked to be alongside Italy’s Parma, Dutch side FC Utrecht and FC Copenhagen of Denmark in targeting Owusu.

Owusu has been a regular in the Foxes’ U18s side for some time and he has stepped up his involvement in the U21s group this season. He is not yet under a professional contract, but that step could come soon having turned 18 earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that owusu has been with Leicester City from a young age, progressing through their academy ranks to the U18s, where he plays most of his football now. Despite only just turning 18, he has already made 54 appearances for the Foxes’ side at the age group.

Sources indicate that his progression and strong performances have seen him make his first four appearances for the U21s this season. Owusu has played in the Premier League Cup and International Cup, alongside one substitute outing in Premier League 2 against Nottingham Forest at the start of November.

The LCFC prospect mainly plays as a winger, but has also been deployed in a central role as an attacking midfielder. He can play on the left or right.

Leicester City have invested huge amounts into their training and academy facilities over the past 10 years. It means they are a great place for young players to hone their craft and develop as players.

Industry observers note that although LCFC would obviously have hoped to be playing far above League One level, the drop has paved the way for some of their brighter academy prospects to break into the senior team. The earlier mentioned trio of Page, Alves and Braybrooke have been among this season’s standout performers.

Jayden Joseph has made nine appearances this term, while Bade Aluko and Tommy Neale have also found opportunities.

It demonstrates players like Owusu that there is a pathway to the first team at the King Power Stadium. They can make the breakthrough they are pursuing with the Foxes, and that can help fend off interest from elsewhere.

Bayern Munich could make a move for the AC Milan target and Club Brugge star Nicolo Tresoldi, following Harry Kane’s injury.

As Milan fans know well after Ardon Jashari and Charles De Ketelaere, it’s notoriously difficult to negotiate with Club Brugge. That means a high offer is needed, which is something that could arrive at the Belgian side’s doorstep in January.

Industry observers note that according to Gazzetta dello Sport, Bayern Munich have been keeping an eye on Tresoldi for some time and initially viewed him as a potential signing for the 2027-28 season. However, due to Harry Kane’s ankle injury, they could move much earlier.

The Englishman will be out for at least three months, having had surgery this morning, and that should keep him sidelined until February/March. That puts Bayern Munich in a difficult spot, perhaps forcing them to make a move in January.

It has been revealed that club Brugge want at least €60m for their star and knowing Bayern Munich’s resources, they would be far more comfortable paying that amount than Milan. In short, Kane’s injury has not only resulted in a headache for the German side, but also for the Rossoneri.

Lionel Messi escapes red card after hurling ball into rival's face in brutal Inter Miami playoff loss

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.
  • It has been revealed that in the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

It has been revealed that in the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Sources indicate that messi then used the ball to shove Tapia's face back. When the Columbus man tried jumping in the air to block the throw, Messi then threw the ball into Tapia's head.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe.

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus.

In a recent development, A frustrated Messi released the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening.

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

Industry observers note that the result has Inter Miami on the brink of elimination from the playoffs after winning the title last season. Columbus dominated every facet of the game, thanks in part to owning 62 percent of possession.

Messi attempted two shots on the evening – counting for half of the saves from Crew keeper Patrick Schulte.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.

#118508. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1802 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sempremilan ↗ Open Full Page

Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.
  • It has been revealed that if we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

It has been revealed that if we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that it won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto).

Sources indicate that some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

Industry observers note that A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

Sources indicate that according to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, presently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

It has been revealed that predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

Industry observers note that they are presently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

According to recent reports, it’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

In a recent development, so, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Recent findings suggest that moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That stated, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

Industry observers note that the last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

It has been revealed that ➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

In a recent development, further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

Industry observers note that as for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That noted, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

24-year-old proves he can ease Kim Hellberg’s worries after starring in Middlesbrough’s win over Swansea City

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that middlesbrough maintained their place at the top of the Championship table on Tuesday night as they defeated managerless Swansea City.
  • Kim Hellberg’s side won 2-1 against the Swans, with Myles Peart-Harris opening the scoring before Joseph Opoku’s equaliser.
  • In a recent development, as well as scoring the first, midfielder Peart-Harris set up Lankshear’s winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that middlesbrough maintained their place at the top of the Championship table on Tuesday night as they defeated managerless Swansea City. It marked back-to-back wins for Boro after the return from the international break, following a 2-0 triumph over Bristol City on Saturday.

Kim Hellberg’s side won 2-1 against the Swans, with Myles Peart-Harris opening the scoring before Joseph Opoku’s equaliser. Star striker Will Lankshear was back amongst the goals to net the second and secure the three points.

In a recent development, as well as scoring the first, midfielder Peart-Harris set up Lankshear’s winner. The 24-year-old started for Middlesbrough and his performance will have come as reassurance for Hellberg given his recent midfield blows.

Earlier this week, Hellberg expressed a desire to reinforce his midfield in the January transfer window. Middlesbrough have lost Rokas Pukstas and Connor Barron to injury, meaning that the only natural players in a deeper role are usual starters Aidan Morris and Sebastian Berhalter.

Peart-Harris, like Riley McGree, can and has played in a deeper role, but is more effective further forward. However, the former Oxford United and Brentford man showed his quality alongside Morris against Swansea City.

According to recent reports, hellberg’s tactics mean Peart-Harris was able to progress into advanced areas. He was lurking in the 18-yard box before being found by Neto Borges’ pull-back and cleverly side-footing into the bottom corner.

For Lankshear’s goal, Peart-Harris just about beat the Swans’ offside trap and ran through before squaring it for the striker to convert. Both goals highlighted the freedom he had to advance, despite being down as one of Hellberg’s deeper midfield players on paper.

Sources indicate that he was able to progress the ball with strong running and forward-thinking passing when in deeper areas. Peart-Harris spent much of the game operating on the right-hand side of the middle third of the pitch, and he was effective for Boro.

In a recent development, hellberg’s lack of depth in midfield is a justified concern, especially coming into the hectic festive schedule. However, Peart-Harris’ performance against Swansea City indicated he is ready to step in for Middlesbrough when Morris and Berhalter need a rest.

It was his best display in a Boro shirt to date, and if he can maintain a high level, he’ll be a valuable squad player to have throughout a demanding 2026/27 promotion push.

The performance doesn’t decrease the need for another midfielder, but it indicates that Hellberg should be able to deal with the shortage until the opportunity to sign a reinforcement arises.
