📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship has already provided some dramatic encounters this season, and many will expect nothing less when Southampton host Middlesbrough on Friday night in front of the Sky cameras.

The past six months tell you there is no love lost between Saints and Boro supporters, which will only add to the atmosphere normally generated when two sides towards the top of the table face off under the lights.

Tonda Eckert's side are just seven points behind the league leaders after 17 matches, and could narrow that gap down to four whilst, in turn, piling the pressure on Wolves, Stoke City and Birmingham City.

There is much to like about the way the German and Kim Hellberg set up their sides, with Boro the undisputed top scorers ahead of the encounter, largely through Will Lankshear's remarkable form.

However, Saints will not be fearful of the quality oozing through Hellberg's ranks, with Eckert also able to call upon several technically gifted individuals in a bid to attack the game.

Eckert is approaching the one-year anniversary of his permanent appointment as Saints head coach, and plenty has gone on since then.

Given the club's recent Premier League past, there is always an expectancy for Saints to be in and among the Championship's promotion hopefuls, and that has remained the case this term despite a four-point deduction.

Home form is seen as a key barometer in the division, and Southampton's displays at St Mary's under the 33-year-old have been almost perfect.

Friday night's clash will be the 30th home fixture Eckert has overseen, with Southampton losing just two of the previous 29 against Hull City on January 17th and to West Ham United in August.

Although Middlesbrough have accumulated one more point and played more times at the Riverside Stadium, Saints, strictly speaking, boast the division's best home record, taking 22 points from a possible 24, scoring 22 goals in the process.

Eckert, who was recently rewarded with a fresh contract, revealed in September that reconnecting with the club's fanbase has been a key reason behind such an impressive run.

As impressive as Middlesbrough have been under Hellberg, the North East outfit aren't flawless, and they were exposed in disappointing away performances and results at Wrexham and Watford.

In both encounters, Boro continued to dominate possession and created 30 openings across 180 minutes, but a lack of cutting edge, somewhat down to an injury sustained by Lankshear, was punished by Phil Parkinson's side, whilst, on another day, a side in better form than the Hornets could have performed a smash-and-grab.

Southampton have averaged 57.1% possession this season, but certainly have the firepower to expose any defensive frailties through the likes of Leo Scienza, Finn Azaz and Canadian hotshot, Cyle Larin, who was back on the goalscoring trail against Derby County.

Boro have also taken just 12 of their 35 points in away matches thus far, which could give travelling supporters further nerves heading into Friday's contest.

With both sides known for a high-tempo game, a fascinating encounter was already on the cards, but then you factor in the passion from the stands which is likely to be channeled by the 22 starters, substitutes and head coaches after May's Spygate debacle.

Hellberg revealed in October that he'd received an apology from Eckert after Southampton were found guilty of breaching EFL regulations and the German was found to have done similar against FA guidelines, but after what ensued in the play-off semi-finals, which were effectively void as Middlesbrough went on to play and lose the final to Hull City in emotionally draining circumstances, the two sets of fans are likely to be partaking in intense 'back-and-forth'.

It has been revealed that who comes out on top in this highly-anticipated fixture? Comment below!

Eckert will hope such feelings are used positively by his team, as one lapse in concentration could bring their unbeaten home record to an end.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Industry observers note that russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

According to recent reports, eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Sources indicate that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian stated. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Industry observers note that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

Industry observers note that tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

According to recent reports, “Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

Industry observers note that “Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

Industry observers note that lewis Hamilton indicates this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

Industry observers note that “It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Significant disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he mentioned he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Sources indicate that excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

It has been revealed that neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

According to recent reports, the championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

According to recent reports, antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one newly introduced set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

Sources indicate that “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he remarked. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

According to recent reports, most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Recent findings suggest that the top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have declared that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Sources indicate that aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who stated the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

Recent findings suggest that “Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti mentioned. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really notable that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

Sources indicate that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the significant upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

Recent findings suggest that with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Industry observers note that formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a fresh floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car enhancement since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

It has been revealed that this race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

At the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

Sources indicate that it will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

With top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Industry observers note that moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Recent findings suggest that finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

Industry observers note that to use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic substantial boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the problems we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

In a recent development, city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Sources indicate that iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

It has been revealed that ‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

It has been revealed that asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – mentioned: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

Recent findings suggest that in Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

It has been revealed that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

Recent findings suggest that in both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

In a recent development, to take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's major boys.

In a recent development, and that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their upcoming manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

It has been revealed that but Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the significant boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Recent findings suggest that iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

Industry observers note that ‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kim Hellberg has Middlesbrough looking like genuine Championship promotion contenders, but his handling of Connor Barron raises some interesting questions for Rangers.

In a recent development, the Scottish midfielder arrived on loan from Ibrox in September, yet has barely featured in Kim Hellberg's plans. Saturday's victory for Middlesbrough over Bristol City in the Championship provided another curious example, with the Boro boss turning to Luke Ayling in midfield.

Sources indicate that that decision came instead of giving Barron an opportunity. Given the work Middlesbrough put into their summer recruitment, and their aspirations of returning to the Premier League, it is a situation worth scrutinising. For Rangers, they will be examining it closely over the next five weeks.

Prior to beating Swansea City last night, Middlesbrough's 2-0 victory over Bristol City was another crucial result in their Championship promotion push, but the substitutions in that game made by Hellberg were particularly interesting.

With Sebastian Berhalter withdrawn in the 77th minute, the Boro boss introduced 35-year-old defender Ayling in his place, seemingly opting for an unconventional midfield solution rather than turning to Barron in a defensive midfield role.

Adilson Malanda has also previously been utilised in midfield despite being a natural centre-back, although this time Hellberg kept him in defence, rather than putting him there and Ayling at the heart of the back four.

The most telling detail is that Barron was not even included in the matchday squad. Having arrived from Rangers on deadline day in September, the 23-year-old has yet to make a single competitive appearance for Middlesbrough.

He has made the bench seven times in all competitions, including six in the league. It is therefore difficult to interpret that as anything other than a worrying sign for his immediate prospects at breaking into Hellberg's looks in a meaningful way at The Riverside.

Recent findings suggest that there is another layer to this situation which makes Hellberg's apparent reluctance to use Barron particularly intriguing. The midfielder's representatives, Every Aspect Group, disclosed when announcing his Middlesbrough move that the agreement includes an option to buy.

Industry observers note that neither club mentioned that clause in their official transfer announcements, making it an interesting detail given the player's current lack of involvement thus far in 2026/27. He has played more for Rangers this season currently, having taken part in UEFA Conference League qualifying.

Per The National, Rangers are also reportedly monitoring his situation ahead of January, and they will hardly be encouraged by what they have seen so far just south of the Scottish border.

If Hellberg does not envisage a role for Barron, there seems little point in allowing the arrangement to continue. A return to Ibrox or another loan or permanent move could become realistic options when the window opens.

However, having played for Rangers this season, if Barron has a single minute of action for Middlesbrough between now and January, then he will be unable to appear for another club again this season. He would only be able to play for Boro or Rangers, with only two clubs permitted per season for a player.

Barron came through Aberdeen's academy, with loan spells at Brechin City and Kelty Hearts helping his development before he established himself in the first-team.

He joined Rangers in 2024, making a significant number of appearances and also gaining European experience with the Scottish giants, but has struggled to secure a regular starting role. He has also represented Scotland at senior level, though, highlighting the potential he is believed to have.

What areas of the squad should Middlesbrough be looking to address in January? Comment below!

According to recent reports, evidently, there is very clearly a capable midfielder there, but perhaps not one suited to Hellberg's requirements. Berhalter and Aidan Morris offer considerably more technical quality and composure in possession, helping Boro dictate proceedings in Championship fixtures. Even Myles Peart-Harris — more of an attacking midfielder — is preferred in holding midfield.

Morris and Berhalter are the primary profiles Hellberg will always prioritise. It is also what they ought to be after in January, rather than persevering with Ayling and Malanda experiments. Therefore, Middlesbrough should let Barron move on and recruit a midfielder who better suits their approach at the base of midfield in the market.

It's taken a little while for Mateus Mane to warm up to the Championship, but the talented teenager is starting to come to the boil for Wolves, which can only be a concern for their fellow promotion hopefuls.

Industry observers note that wolves have gone under the radar for the most part in their second-tier return so far. Cesar Peixoto is still not the most popular manager in Wolverhampton, but the Old Gold are cruising through certain games this season.

They momentarily climbed into the top two on Tuesday night after a convincing 3-0 win over a Derby County side in disarray, and have now won five of their last six, including both after coming back from the international break.

What's more exciting, though, is that Mane has come back from the break on red-hot form and is finally seeing things go his way. For someone who had a £50 million price tag slapped on him earlier this year, we're finally starting to see why.

Mane was a rare bright spark in an otherwise dismal season at Molineux last year. The Portuguese wideman was brought to the forefront by Rob Edwards, and gave a Wolves side who were doomed after two points through 18 games a much-needed boost.

He scored and assisted in their first league win of the campaign against West Ham United back in January, and followed that up with another goal in a 1-1 draw against Everton just days later.

According to recent reports, at that point, Wolves were destined for the drop, but now they had an 18-year-old superstar who could continue his career at the top level. Liverpool and Manchester United were two of the big clubs interested, but reports in late February hinted that the Old Gold wanted £50 million for him.

In the end, a combination of that price tag putting suitors off, and Mane himself being happy to develop in the Championship for a year, meant that he stayed at Molineux, and after five goal contributions in a terrible Premier League side, he was primed for a massive year in a second-tier outfit expected to challenge right at the top.

A year in the Championship can be good for a side to reset and return to the Premier League in a stronger position. For Mane, it would have given him the opportunity to be one of the best players in the league, if things worked out, and build his confidence ahead of a career in the top flight.

Ultimately, that wasn't the case, and the second-tier proved difficult to begin with for the 19-year-old.

The first game of the season against Blackburn Rovers was a bit of a culture shock for the club as a whole, but definitely for Mane, who was often found needing to offer more defensively against Ryan Alebiosu off the Rovers' right, and was subbed after an hour with the side 2-1 down.

From then on, he began to get into his groove, completing dribbles and getting into shooting positions, but not having the end product needed to profit from those, which was a significant frustration and a little alarming for those who expected him to go from strength to strength at this level.

Peixoto even dropped Mane after back-to-back defeats against Middlesbrough and Bolton Wanderers, with latest arrival Rafiki Noted taking the left-wing spot after he returned from an early injury, and the 19-year-old found himself coming off the bench four times in a five-game run.

Said has kept his place on the left, but Mane has now been deployed on the right for the last two games, and it's starting to work wonders for the Portuguese starlet.

Mane is finding that end product both in terms of creating chances and finally scoring his first goal of the season with what was his 39th shot of the campaign in the win against Derby on Tuesday night.

Industry observers note that but the excellence began against Charlton Athletic on Saturday. The 19-year-old played off the right and began the game by spurning a major chance. At the time, he had yet to score, and many were feeling he was simply cursed at this level.

It has been revealed that mane responded by just setting up goals instead, though. He assisted both in the 2-1 win over the Addicks, taking his tally to three for the season, and created seven chances and four big chances in a Man of the Match display.

In a recent development, he was able to follow that up against the Rams, too. It was his incredible skill which led to Adam Armstrong's opener; he could have grabbed at least one assist, too, before he then got his goal to put Wolves two to the good.

Sources indicate that do you think that this is a turning point for Mateus Mane? Let us know in the comments.

Recent findings suggest that that's now three goal involvements in two games, when he had just one in the previous 15. If this is a sign of things to come, fellow title-challengers, such as Middlesbrough, Birmingham City, Stoke City and Southampton, need to be aware.

Granted, these performances have come against two of the poorer sides in the division so far, and with Lincoln City on the horizon on Saturday, we won't know if Mane is now a force to be reckoned with against top teams, but it's promising for the 19-year-old.

It has been revealed that as mentioned, his strike against Derby was his 39th shot of the season. Only 10 players in the entire league have had more, per Opta. So, it's not been for a lack of trying, and he's been the victim of some bad luck, too.

Hopefully, that goal can open up the floodgates and the Portuguese wideman can be more of a threat.

According to recent reports, in terms of chance creation, too, the 14 he's made over the past two games have shot him up those ranks. Now, only four players can say they've created more, and only Finn Azaz and Jarrod Bowen can say they have in open play.

It has been revealed that time will tell whether this is the start of a real breakthrough into Championship superstardom for Mane. If it is, a Wolves side who were already projecting as one of the best sides in the league could get even better.

The owner fully immersed himself in the Milan world again: he spoke with his transfer team, with the team about the match against Frosinone, and with Ruben Amorim about both topics.

Tech Report: Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?
  • Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling newly introduced era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool.

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

It has been revealed that the fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

Sources indicate that his assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

There were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

He is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better.

Sources indicate that liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

It helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

It has been revealed that the German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

According to recent reports, and that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The League One season is only three-and-a-half months old, but some sides are already starting to prove their worth as potential promotion candidates come May.

Last term, there was no real jeopardy for some time over Lincoln City and Cardiff City's runs to automatic promotion, with the Imps winning the division at a 12-point canter, whilst a staggering 14 points separated the Bluebirds and Stockport County, who went on to lose the play-off final to Bolton Wanderers.

As the final matchday of November 2026 looms, there are only 10 points separating second-placed Huddersfield Town and Wycombe Wanderers, who currently find themselves 15th.

Sources indicate that it is anyone's game to predict who will gain promotion to the Championship, but with finances playing such a key role in the progression of clubs in the EFL, what are the added incentives on the line? Football League World takes a look...

The EFL's current broadcasting deal means that clubs across the Championship, League One and League Two receive a share of £187m, although divisional status plays a huge role in how much is received on an individual basis.

In May 2025, it was reported that the 24 clubs in League One are receiving £2m a season in prize money, which is approximately £500,000 more than their counterparts in League Two.

However, as many ambitious clubs from the recent past can attest to, returning to the Championship can change everything, with those in the second tier receiving up to £11m, which comes through basic costs and further solidarity payments from the Premier League.

Stockport currently lead the way in League One, with Jimmy McNulty's side winning their last three encounters, attributing to a total of 32 points from 16 matches.

Martin Drury's first months as Huddersfield boss have also gone according to initiative, as Town have a game in hand on their promotion rivals right now, and in Derensili Sanches Fernandes, arguably have the division's hottest property, whilst the goalscoring exploits of Joe Taylor, as Football League World exclusively revealed, has attracted interest from Burnley and Swansea City.

In a recent development, who will win promotion from League One this season? Comment below!

Oxford United are right now the highest-placed side out of the three who were relegated from last season's Championship, with Aaron Ramsey getting a fine tune out of his players at the Kassam Stadium despite the fact the club continues to operate under a transfer embargo.

At present, Opta predict that the top three will remain the same after 46 games, with Huddersfield's expected points total just 0.19 higher than that of Oxford's, which would be some finish to the season.

The January transfer window is certain to have implications on the promotion race, and given the pre-season expectations which surrounded the two clubs, both Leicester City and Sheffield Wednesday will also hope to be in the promotion conversation.

Foxes fans were extremely critical of Russell Martin's possession-based style earlier in the campaign, but his side has lost just one of their last six League One outings, which included a standout victory at Huddersfield last weekend.

Wednesday, meanwhile, are at the moment unbeaten in their opening three league encounters under former Stockport boss, Dave Challinor, but a sixth draw of the season against Stevenage further echoed the need for potential attacking signings when January comes around.

The League Two season is now well underway, and as expected, English football's fourth tier hasn't disappointed when it comes to the drama which has already been provided.

It will come as no surprise to learn that the top-half of the table is extremely congested as the campaign nears its halfway point, with several sides now hopeful that they can be the ones who mount a successful promotion bid to League One, with three automatic spots up for grabs as well as the eventual play-off victors at Wembley Stadium.

In order to achieve such strong short-term goals, a full squad effort will be required right until matchday 46, and many individuals have already been in the limelight for their exploits this term.

It comes as no surprise that the majority of those come in the form of attacking stars, but having a resolute goalkeeper certainly goes a long way for any head coach.

With that in mind, according to Transfermarkt's current valuations, which 20 League Two shot-stoppers are the most valuable? FLW takes a look.

It has been revealed that this list is NOT based on FLW's opinion, it's based on Transfermarkt's valuations. All figures converted from Euros to GBP.

Will Brook is now in the thick of his second campaign at Shrewsbury Town, having joined from Leamington FC in August 2025.

The Shropshire outfit have endured mixed fortunes since the 23-year-old's arrival, but after signing a fresh two-and-a-half year contract in November 2025, his current market value is noted to be £104,711.

Next up is Newport County's mainstay between the sticks, Jordan Wright, who moved to the South Wales outfit in the summer of 2025 from divisional rivals, Grimsby Town.

The Nottingham Forest academy graduate is certainly well experienced in both League One and League Two, having made over 100 appearances across the two divisions.

Since joining the Exiles, Wright has already accumulated a double-figure tally of clean sheets, contributing to a current £125,621 valuation.

Another shot-stopper valued at £125,621 right now is 27-year-old Taye Ashby-Hammond, who signed for Barnet on a free transfer in June.

The former England youth international previously won promotion out of the division with Stevenage, and given the Bees' bright start under Dean Brennan, similar exploits could be achieved in May at The Hive.

Zach Jeacock is also worth £125,621 at this stage of the season after joining Northampton Town on loan from current Championship side, Lincoln City.

The former England youth international and Birmingham City academy graduate has made a solid start to life at Sixfields, conceding the joint-second fewest goals per 90 minutes on average.

Harvey Cartwright returned to Grimsby Town on loan this summer from Premier League newcomers, Hull City, having spent time at Blundell Park during the 2023/24 campaign.

After keeping five clean sheets in 25 League Two matches back then, the 24-year-old is currently a deputy in David Artell's squad, but has still retained a market valuation of £125,621.

Ahead of Cartwright is his Mariners teammate and the vastly experienced Christy Pym, with the 31-year-old's current market valuation sitting in the region of £146,540.

The man, who is closing in on 300 appearances at League Two level, signed a two-year deal in North-East Lincolnshire last summer, and has retained his starting berth despite just six clean sheets in all competitions last term, as well as a remarkable display in the historic EFL Cup triumph over Manchester United.

Alfie McNally is also worth £146,540 in the current market, with the 21-year-old signing for York City on loan from Premier League side, Fulham, this summer.

The Londoner has certainly performed to an admirable standard in what is his first taste of senior football, whilst he remains under contract at Craven Cottage until June 2028.

Cheltenham Town's Wyll Stanway is one of three goalkeepers on this list with a valuation of £167,490.

The brother of England Lioness, Georgia, signed for the Robins this summer from Barrow after the Bluebirds' relegation to the National League, and has certainly been busy, averaging the third-highest number of saves per 90.

Bristol Rovers' campaign has been one of frustration, with Steve Evans' position under increasing pressure as a result.

However, the Gas could be in an even worse position were it not for the services of £167,490-valued goalkeeper, Brad Young, who signed from Leicester City in June 2025.

The 24-year-old currently ranks as one of the best in the division when it comes to clean sheets.

Also valued at £167,490 is Crewe Alexandra goalkeeper, Tom Booth.

The 24-year-old has progressed through the Railwaymen's highly-rated academy system and into the first-team fold, and since his debut in April 2023, has amassed over 60 appearances.

Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen is reportedly open to a move to Manchester United, although any potential transfer would depend on an agreement with the Turkish champions.

According to recent reports, the Nigeria international, 27, has been linked with United as latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino considers his attacking options. According to The Sun, Osimhen is flattered by the reported interest and remains keen to play in the Premier League during his career. However, there has been no confirmation of a formal approach or negotiations between the clubs.

Sources indicate that osimhen is under contract until June 2029 and reportedly earns around £13m a year. The Sun indicates Galatasaray value the former Napoli forward at between £80m and £100m, with the club reluctant to lose him midway through the season.

According to recent reports, the report also suggests there is no release clause in his contract, meaning United would need to agree a fee with Galatasaray. A source described as close to Osimhen told the newspaper that the striker was flattered by the interest but remained loyal to his current club. Any January move could therefore prove difficult, with a summer transfer potentially more realistic.

In a recent development, osimhen has scored 10 goals in 11 appearances across all competitions this season, following campaigns of 37 and 22 goals for Galatasaray. His reported interest in a Premier League move comes as Pochettino prepares for his first match in charge of United against Liverpool on Sunday.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury has reduced United’s attacking options, while Joshua Zirkzee has struggled to establish himself as a regular goalscorer. The speculation was also included in Sky Sports’ transfer paper talk, which attributed the claims to The Sun. For now, Osimhen remains a Galatasaray player, with no indication that a transfer is close.

Middlesbrough remained top of the Championship after a dominant 2-1 win over managerless Swansea City, but the substantial news came in the lineup, as Will Lankshear made his return to the eleven.

Sources indicate that lankshear has been so vital to Boro so far this season, scoring 13 in 13 league games before he went down with a hamstring problem ahead of the international break. In the two outings he missed, Kim Hellberg's side picked up one point and scored no goals.

Middlesbrough demonstrated that they could score without him on Saturday, as they were already 2-0 up against Bristol City before he came on with 13 minutes to go, but he proved vital back in the starting eleven on Tuesday night, netting the winner to take his tally to 14 in 15 games.

What was arguably more notable, though, was that he came back to form a strike partnership, as Kim Hellberg played two up top for the first time this season.

It has been revealed that hellberg has played two up top before as Middlesbrough boss, but for the most part has gone with a lone striker, especially this season. With Lankshear leading the line perfectly, there hasn't been the need to put more strikers into the lineup.

In the 21-year-old's absence, the Swedish boss opted for David Strelec, and he repaid his faith with his first of the season in that 2-0 win over the Robins at the Riverside on Saturday.

With Lankshear coming back, though, many expected the Slovakian international to drop to the bench, but that wasn't the case. The 25-year-old started alongside the prolific marksman, and both played an hour together.

That could indicate what Hellberg wants to do with them both fit. The Swansea game was arguably the first time this season with them both ready to start together, with Strelec enduring an injury-troubled start to the campaign while Lankshear was firing on all cylinders, and hitting fitness when the 21-year-old went down with that hamstring problem.

Ultimately, the demand for somebody like Lankshear to come in and lead the line was only there amongst Boro fans because of their wastefulness in front of goal last season, which was one of the major factors in them missing out on promotion, and Strelec played his part in that.

The Slovakian was one of Middlesbrough's marquee signings ahead of last season, arriving for an initial £6.5 million from Slovan Bratislava late on in the summer window.

The year before, he'd scored 25 in 48 appearances in all competitions, including a couple in the UEFA Champions League, one of which was against Atlético Madrid, and had already netted five in nine for his former side in the infancy of the campaign before the move.

It has been revealed that at the Riverside, though, he struggled to make an immediate impact at Championship level. He scored eight goals in around 1,850 minutes, three of which came in the final four games of the season, underperforming his expected goals tally.

But it's often the case that foreign forwards need a little bit of time to acclimatise to the level; look at Andri Gudjohnsen and Zan Vipotnik in the past couple of years, and the Boro boss is definitely not writing Strelec off after last season.

Kim Hellberg has ensured that he hasn't ruled out the possibility of playing Strelec alongside Lankshear this season, believing that if he can prove his worth in the side in training and in games, he can force that tweak in formation which we saw on Tuesday night.

Back in late October, when the 25-year-old was revealed to be back in training, Hellberg admitted that "David has top, top qualities, and we will need them. I don't see a problem playing with two strikers; I see a possibility to do that.".

Then, after he scored against Bristol City in the game in which Lankshear returned, the Swedish boss reaffirmed the possibility of the duo playing up front together in the future.

Recent findings suggest that "Absolutely. I don't think there's any problem playing both of them," he stated. "Like I say, we're trying to find solutions all the time for the best players and players that perform. Absolutely, David and Will could be fantastic together.".

Evidently, Hellberg hasn't given up on him, and neither have the Middlesbrough fans, who serenaded the Slovakian after he scored against the Robins, and were pleased to see him start up front with Lankshear in midweek.

Industry observers note that obviously, with the change in shape, there were some teething concerns. Hellberg spoke after the win that he felt that Lankshear was drifting out wide a bit too much, but the 15 minutes they spent on the pitch after the break were brilliant, and the 21-year-old got his goal.

If the pairing can form a strong relationship on the pitch, an already dangerous frontline at the Riverside could prove to be unstoppable between now and May.

Do you think Kim Hellberg will settle on a two-up-top formation this season? Let us know in the comments.

Having the goalscoring prowess of Lankshear should take some of the pressure off Strelec, too, you'd hope, which could lead him to be more clinical than he was in front of goal last season.

The 25-year-old could find himself settling into life in the EFL a lot quicker, which can only be a positive for Boro's promotion chances. If they can have two sharp-shooters leading the line, there may be no relinquishing the top spot for Kim Hellberg's side this year.

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

Sources indicate that england’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

It has been revealed that but here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Industry observers note that the concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. Loud (high-pitched) cheers for the Croatia team from children inside the Rijeka Stadium. Luka Modric, aged 41, is starting for the home team. He’s a year older than Wayne Rooney, who retired from international football nine years ago. The England players were booed when they entered the pitch. These kids know what they are doing.

Industry observers note that I was here eight years ago when it really was a behind-closed-doors game for England. This is very different. There are around 6,000 Croatian children, with their guardians, here and the stands are filling up. It’s also pretty noisy with all the pre-match music.

In 2018, we could hear exactly what the managers and players were shouting – Jordan Henderson was particularly loud – but I don’t think that will be the case this time around. The noise from the fans may be quite high pitched today, but I don’t think it will be quiet at all.

According to recent reports, england have 100 fans here and, mercifully, they have not been forced to watch from inside the metal caged away end. They haven’t been allowed to bring in England flags, so it’s currently quite hard to locate exactly where they are.

Croatia Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Perisic; Modric, Kovacic; Ivanovic, P Sucic, Baturina; Musa.Substitutes Pandur, Kotarski, Smolcic, Sutalo, Kramaric, Vlasic, Mario Pasalic, Jakic, Marco Pasalic, Matanovic, Luka Sucic, Misic.

England Pickford; Quansah, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall; Anderson, Scott; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.Substitutes Trafford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Chalobah, Ngumoha, Branthwaite, Lewis-Skelly, Rogers, Garner, Calvert-Lewin, Gibbs-White, Eze.

Referee Sven Jablonski (Germany).

Thomas Tuchel was glowing about Alex Scott in his pre-match media duties ahead of today’s game against Croatia and the midfielder has been handed his first England start.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Tuchel had taken Scott to the United States on his pre-World Cup training camp, but the Bournemouth midfielder was not part of the squad for the tournament-proper.

In a recent development, on Scott, Tuchel remarked: “I am super impressed by Alex Scott, I think he is at the moment one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and he just proves it in every training session. He had a fantastic debut the other day and really really impressed me.”.

Recent findings suggest that 🇭🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Croatia's starting XI vs. England!Petar Musa and Martin Baturina get their first starts under Slaven Bilić! pic.twitter.com/dPt32fiXbh.

Your #ThreeLions for Saturday night 🔴🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/A2M4lMfBNj.

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has stated Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s newly introduced goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

In a recent development, jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

In a recent development, uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

In a recent development, thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.
