📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s most creative player since his arrival to the club in 2020.

According to recent reports, the 32-year-old is approaching the final months of his current deal, which expires at the end of the season. United do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, keeping him at Old Trafford until 2028.

While they can extend his contract for a year, Manchester United are actively pursuing a deal to tie Bruno Fernandes beyond 2028.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a fresh contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

Fernandes confirmed that an offer had been made but dismissed suggestions that he was holding out for a better salary or a longer agreement.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

He also insisted that money has never been the reason behind his decision to remain at United, despite having opportunities to move elsewhere in previous transfer windows.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes remarked.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”.

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting in 2020. He has scored 75 Premier League goals for the club and set a new competition record for assists in a single season last term.

Recent findings suggest that bruno’s comments don’t sound like he is holding United hostage demanding more pay or refusing to sign a new one. The intention as told by Bruno Fernandes just show his leadership trait about putting the team first. He has no immediate intention of making his contract situation the centre of attention. That will be a sign of encouragement for the fans as well.

Manchester United need to start winning games again. When they do and surely Bruno Fernandes will be at the centre of it, the contract talks can resume and take priority.

Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he noted as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Recent findings suggest that wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season.

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

It has been revealed that the 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

Klopp can’t take any credit for that.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield.

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED.

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the latest manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

Recent findings suggest that none of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a big defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United.

It has been revealed that the two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

Sources indicate that but that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

According to recent reports, there was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

Recent findings suggest that but Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at significant clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has noted he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

According to recent reports, nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday.

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker revealed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

Sources indicate that he signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

In a recent development, palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

LONG ROAD AHEAD FOR THE NEW KID.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With substantial money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, currently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history.

Of the new managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical challenges stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

In a recent development, lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a fresh contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof.

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

The fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City's eight years outside the Premier League have been a rather mixed experience, with the club struggling to rediscover the consistency and ambition that once made them such an established top-flight outfit.

It has been revealed that since Graham Potter's arrival in 2018, following their relegation, the Swans have experienced some encouraging highs but plenty of frustrating lows. However, those lows have been better than many of their Championship peers, having finished in the bottom half of the Championship just twice.

Sources indicate that in fact, Swansea City placed 15th in 2021/22 and 14th in 2023/24, while their four other finishes have seen them end 10th or 11th. Their best opportunities for a return to the Premier League came from 2019–2021, after one particular manager guided them into the play-offs in consecutive campaigns, finishing sixth and then fourth.

Swansea remain an ambitious club with genuine aspirations of returning to the Premier League, but they lack the financial muscle and resources of many Championship rivals. Their recruitment budget, wage structure, and ability to retain their best players can all hold them back, particularly when competing against clubs with parachute payments and greater spending power.

Sources indicate that that said, there had also been genuine optimism surrounding the club again this season, with Vitor Matos overseeing an encouraging start that had Swansea competing around the automatic promotion places in 2026/27. However, his recent departure for Ligue 1 side Strasbourg has thrown their campaign into uncertainty, leaving the club searching for another permanent appointment recently.

It would be unfair to judge them until they have had 10 games or more in charge, but now, with seven permanent managers having taken charge since Potter's arrival and until Matos' exit, it feels an appropriate time to assess how each has performed and rank them from worst to best.

Who is your favourite Swansea manager of the modern era? Comment below!

According to recent reports, it is hard to look past Alan Sheehan as the bottom-placed pick of the seven here. While the Irishman deserves plenty of credit for steady caretaker spells — including that five-game winning streak in early 2025 that landed him the permanent gig with Swansea — the step up to full-time Championship management proved to be a bridge too far for him and he didn't make it far into 2025/26 after taking on his first senior role.

Appointed on a three-year deal in April 2025, his tenure unravelled alarmingly swiftly once the pressure of expectations set in. Managing just four league wins from the opening 15 games of the 2025/26 campaign, his side looked devoid of identity, culminating in a dismal 4-1 home defeat to Ipswich Town. Without a distinct tactical blueprint or the pull to attract interest from elsewhere, Sheehan's permanent spell was a textbook case of the interim bounce fading fast.

Sources indicate that on paper, Michael Duff arrived at the Swansea.com Stadium with serious pedigree after guiding Barnsley to the League One play-off final. In reality, however, his appointment was a complete cultural mismatch from day one. Swansea supporters take immense pride in their possession-heavy, progressive footballing identity, yet Duff immediately pivoted toward a more direct, physical approach that saw possession figures plummet and fans swiftly turn.

Industry observers note that playing 'The Swansea Way' is just one factor, though. With just 21 points collected from 19 league matches — the club's worst return at that stage since 2018 — and a miserable run of one win in eight, the hierarchy had little choice but to pull the plug after five months. Duff is a fine EFL operator, as shown by his subsequent stints at Huddersfield Town, Wycombe Wanderers, and now at Bradford City; but he was never right for SA1.

In a recent development, luke Williams edges ahead of Duff primarily because he actually understood what Swansea City are supposed to look like on a football pitch. Having previously worked as Russell Martin’s assistant and torn up the lower tiers with a hyper-attacking Notts County side, Williams returned to South Wales in January 2024 with a clear commitment to front-foot, possession-based football. There were genuine flashes of quality during his 13 months at the helm, and he steadied the ship effectively in the second half of the 2023/24 campaign.

Ultimately, though, a lack of ruthlessness in both boxes proved to be his undoing. His side had streaks of strong form to look like serious challengers to the top six, but also poor runs far from their purple patch best. A bleak run after the turn of the year in early 2025 saw Swansea slide toward trouble, leading to his dismissal in February. Respectable, stylistically aligned, yet ultimately unable to sustain momentum.

Sources indicate that graham Potter may have only spent 11 months in South Wales, yet his impact on the club’s modern identity was profound. Inheriting a bloated and demoralised squad following Premier League relegation in 2018, Potter stripped things back, promoted fearless academy graduates like Dan James and Connor Roberts, and restored 'The Swansea Way' in breathtaking fashion. They may not have made the play-offs in their first Championship campaign after relegation, but building blocks were put in place by Potter.

According to recent reports, A tenth-place Championship finish and a thrilling FA Cup quarter-final clash with Manchester City only told half the story; Swansea played some of the most fluid, intelligent football in and out of possession in the second tier. Unsurprisingly, Brighton & Hove Albion swooped in to prise him away in May 2019, and his subsequent rise to Chelsea and international management underlines just how elite a tactician Swansea had on their hands. Given their young core, Potter could have achieved plenty with more time at the club.

Arguably the most debatable positioning when comparing him to Potter, as few managers have polarised opinion in SA1 quite like Russell Martin, yet his place on the podium is thoroughly deserved. Across nearly two years in charge, Martin doubled down on extreme possession-based principles, producing some unforgettable afternoons — none more so than completing Swansea’s first-ever South Wales derby double over Cardiff City.

In a recent development, while his stubbornness occasionally led to frustrating defensive lapses, he oversaw clear year-on-year progression, guiding the Swans to a 10th-place finish in 2022/23 while developing stars like Joel Piroe and Nathan Wood. When newly-relegated Southampton paid compensation to make him the centerpiece of their Premier League promotion push in June 2023, it served as ultimate validation of his methods and upside when given the time and resources.

Recent findings suggest that few managers have transformed the mood in SA1 quite as dramatically as Vitor Matos. Inheriting a confidence-shot side from Alan Sheehan in November 2025, the Portuguese tactician immediately injected high-octane pressing, technical sharpness, and clear tactical structure to rescue the 2025/26 campaign. Armed with a full summer window and working alongside Jamestown Analytics’ data-led recruitment model, Matos elevated Swansea into genuine top-six contenders.

They were playing exhilarating, progressive football that had the Swans firmly on course for at least a first play-off finish since the Steve Cooper era. That trajectory was only halted because Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, backed by BlueCo’s financial muscle, moved decisively to poach him in recent weeks. Had he stayed in South Wales, a top-six Championship berth felt virtually assured, making second place thoroughly deserved.

Recent findings suggest that there is simply no debating top spot. Steve Cooper remains the gold standard of Swansea's post-Premier League era, delivering back-to-back Championship play-off finishes in 2019/20 and 2020/21 — including a trip to the Wembley final — despite operating under strict financial constraints and constant squad turnover. While his pragmatic, counter-attacking setup wasn't always purist 'Swansea Way' football, Cooper possessed a rare knack for squeezing every ounce of quality out of players.

He used his England youth connections to get plenty out of loan signings like Rhian Brewster, Marc Guehi, Morgan Gibbs-White, and Conor Gallagher. He made the Swans fiercely difficult to beat and instilled a winning mentality that hasn't been matched since. His subsequent achievements taking Nottingham Forest back to the Premier League only cement his status as the standout boss on this list. Perhaps Matos could have surpassed him had he remained in charge, but Cooper simply has to top the seven.

According to The Sun’s report, published on Saturday evening, United’s players have already noticed longer and more intense training sessions compared with those under former manager Michael Carrick.

In a recent development, the newspaper reports that Pochettino has initially concentrated on introducing his tactical approach, with more demanding physical work expected once the Liverpool fixture is over. In a recent development, pochettino’s first assignment is Sunday’s visit to Anfield, with United looking to improve on a difficult opening to the Premier League season. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager conducted an extended training session on Saturday as preparations for the fixture continued.

In a recent development, however, the reported emphasis on fitness and conditioning suggests that his wider changes at Carrington may become more apparent after the Liverpool match. United have not publicly confirmed the details of the training programme described in the report.

Breaking: Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.
  • With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.
  • United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Industry observers note that andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

According to recent reports, juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United have found life back in the Championship for the first time in over a decade a struggle to adapt to, as new head coach Scott Parker must utilise the January transfer window to set things right in East London.

Upon their relegation to the Championship last season, West Ham haven't exactly had the start to life back in the second tier as they would've hoped for.

The Hammers failed to win any of their first three games in charge, and after a poor string of results, Nuno Espírito Santo was replaced at the helm by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker hasn't fared much better as yet, failing to win any of his four games in charge against Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End, and Portsmouth, and in the past couple of games, the 46-year-old boss has made a big team selection decision.

Danish shot-stopper Mads Hermansen has endured a tricky time at West Ham, joining the club in the summer of 2025 for around £20 million from Leicester City, and spent his first year at the club battling Alphonse Areola for a place between the sticks.

Upon their relegation, Hermansen has since become the Hammers' undisputed number one, at least up until recently, as according to FotMob, the 26-year-old has allowed in 4.24 more goals than expected at this stage, subsequently being dropped for 20-year-old Finlay Herrick.

Herrick, who had only ever played in the National League for Boreham Wood before his introduction to the first team in the past couple of games, has been thrust into the deep end by Parker and has struggled to adapt to life in the Championship.

With Hermansen not trusted, Herrick inexperienced, and Areola last making a competitive appearance back in April, a newly introduced number one should be on the cards this winter, as an obvious option is surely right in front of them.

It was reported by Alan Nixon via Patreon earlier in November that Parker was looking to add another left-back and centre-forward to his ranks at West Ham, with the former England and Hammers midfielder already looking ahead to January.

He will need to turn results around quickly; otherwise, he may not make it to the end of the year as things stand, and if he does indeed turn the tide at the London Stadium, a upcoming goalkeeper must become a priority, as Derby County's Jacob Widell Zetterström should be targeted.

Zetterström, 28, according to FotMob, has kept out 3.63 more goals than expected at this stage, and continued to outperform his expected numbers despite Derby's struggles at the foot of the division.

A fully-fledged Swedish international, often battling Stoke City's Viktor Johansson for the gloves in Graham Potter's national team, Zetterström is in his prime years as a goalkeeper, and still may well have some of his best displays ahead of him, as one key contract factor could make this deal a lot easier to complete for the Hammers.

Zetterström joined Derby in the summer of 2024, having spent the entirety of his career to that date in his native Sweden with Djurgarden, and ever since his move to Pride Park, has been the club's undisputed number one.

Signing a three-year deal, the terms that the 28-year-old signed some two-and-a-half years ago are due to expire next summer, with no indication as to whether he will sign an extension as yet.

Premier League outfit Leeds United were interested in signing the Swede over the summer, whilst Italian top-flight side Monza reportedly registered an interest, as the Rams stood firm.

With Derby in a relegation battle at the foot of the division, Rams boss John Eustace will be incredibly reluctant to lose his star shot-stopper before the end of the season, but with a serious risk of losing him for nothing, he may have no other choice but to sell, especially if an acceptable offer arrives.

West Ham certainly have the money to tempt him away from Pride Park, and for a cut-price fee, Parker can secure one of the Championship's best this winter and fix a key problem area in the process.

Industry observers note that do you think West Ham should look to sign Zetterström from Derby this winter, or should they be looking elsewhere? How much would it take to sign the Swede this winter? Share your thoughts below!

With four games without a win to begin his tenure in East London, Parker is quickly realising the gravity of the task laid out before him, and will be hoping to get around to the January window ASAP.

It's clear the Hammers lack a trusted shot-stopper as things stand, and as one of his first actions this winter, the 46-year-old must look to fix this as soon as possible to instil some confidence into his back line.

With Burnley, Parker could rely upon James Trafford to perform beyond expectations - with West Ham, he doesn't have that luxury, and he should look to fix this in the form of Zetterström this winter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Sources indicate that pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the fresh head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

According to recent reports, the Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

The defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical blueprint was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the issues exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

Industry observers note that keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Summerville, meanwhile, fits the younger, explosive one-v-one profile that would sit neatly inside Alonso’s longer-term wing plan.

Read Chelsea has already tracked the separate Summerville angle, but this latest dual link sharpens the picture.

Chelsea appear to be testing two different solutions to the same problem: proven reliability or higher-upside acceleration.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (480 w)

Breaking: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (480 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heading into the busy festive period, Huddersfield Town remain firmly in the automatic promotion mix.

There’s not been too much to complain about for those connected with the Yorkshire outfit, with the Terriers already netting 28 goals so far this term with such a sharp front line, while they have also conceded the fewest goals in the division, a recipe for success when it comes to getting back into the Championship.

From their opening 15 league games, Martin Drury’s men have only tasted defeat twice so far this campaign, with eight victories in the process, leaving them in a handy position to challenge and get into top spot over Christmas.

You’ve got to feel Huddersfield stand a great chance of returning to the Championship come the end of the season, but a massive hurdle to navigate in order to achieve that is by hanging on to their most prized assets, with some of those bound to be subject to transfer speculation in January after producing superb performances week in, week out.

One in particular is Huddersfield forward Joe Taylor, who has dazzled so far this season and heavily contributed to the Terriers being in a promising position to achieve automatic promotion.

But with links to some Championship clubs at the turn of the new year, an exit for the 24-year-old has the potential to shake up the promotion race completely, with the Terriers' hierarchy having a big decision to make if a concrete offer is tabled.

From a Huddersfield Town perspective, so much credit has to go to Welsh forward Joe Taylor for the start the Terriers have made this season.

Versatile enough to flip between playing as a number 10 and as a lone striker, Taylor has already got into double figures for goals from the 14 league games he’s played in, nailing himself down as one of the first names on the team sheet due to such a clinical nature in the final third.

Taylor has been part of such an electric forward line, with himself and Derensili Sanches Fernandes at the heart of most of their good work, with that duo in particular needing to sustain their form over the whole of the campaign if they are to get the club back into the second tier.

And with goals flowing from Taylor in the early stages of the term, it’s no surprise to see him linked with making a step-up back to the Championship, with some transfer speculation emerging about the forward heading into the January window that may worry the Yorkshire outfit.

An exclusive report from us here at Football League World has revealed that second tier duo Burnley and Swansea City are both eyeing up moves for Taylor to bolster their frontlines heading into the second portion of the season.

Swansea, of course, lost head coach Vitor Matos to Strasbourg last week, but it will not stop them eyeing up targets ahead of January, and Taylor is on their radar, as they are looking at adding him to a strike-force consisting of Adam Idah, Ross Stewart and Zan Vipotnik.

Burnley, meanwhile, find themselves in a relegation battle under Fabio Celestini and may need some further additions at the top end of the pitch to get them out of the mire, with current centre-forward options like Jamie Vardy, Zeki Amdouni and Andreas Hountondji, failing to provide a consistent return of goals.

So with this in mind, FLW’s Huddersfield fan pundit has reacted to the latest links and how much the club should demand for Taylor's services in January.

Speaking to Football League World, Huddersfield Town fan pundit Graeme Rayner has demanded that the Terriers accept nothing less than £10m from Burnley or Swansea City for Joe Taylor in January, admitting that while it is a ‘laughably massive’ fee for a League One player, they can’t lose a player who has such an impact on their automatic promotion ambitions.

Graeme told FLW: “Until this season, Joe Taylor’s career at Town hadn’t come to life. He went on loan to Wigan for the second half of last season, demonstrated what he can do if you use him in the right way and if you supply him in the right way, and since then he’s come back and been absolutely superb this season for Huddersfield.

“He’s on 10 goals already, and we’re only in November, late November, he’s been featured in the Wales squad, although he hasn’t got any minutes, but he’s kicked on, and he is one of the reasons, and there are many of them, but one of the key reasons why Huddersfield are right in the hunt for automatic promotion and definitely for the play-offs.”.

Asked about the fee Huddersfield should demand for Taylor, Graeme added: “On Saturday we played at home to Leicester, he played, and neither him nor Derensili Sanches Fernandes were on their best game, and it revealed, and it showed how reliant upon them both we have become for that cutting edge up front, so to answer your question, if somebody wants to come in January and take away our top goalscorer, then they’re going to have to pay through the nose for that.

“Strikers in January are always extra expensive, British strikers carry a premium as well, and both of those factors, plus the likely impact on us, mean it would have to be silly money and a fee that’s so massive that it’s laughably big and we have to take it.

“I would say it would have to be an eight-figure sum. If I’m the chairman of Huddersfield and I’m thinking we’ve been in League One for too long, and have to get back in the Championship, the value of us keeping Joe Taylor to get us back in the Championship is more than his actual paper value, so don’t offer us anything less than £10m.

Huddersfield Town fans, do you agree that the Terriers shouldn't accept anything under £10m for Joe Taylor in January? Leave your thoughts in the comments below!

“Now that might sound fanciful, but Birmingham’s signing of Jay Stansfield for £15m the other season in League One has possibly shifted the goalposts anyway, but it’s about him being worth more to us than just his transfer value, so if they came in with less than £10m then I’d laugh them out the door.

“But I do hope that we’ve already been scouting out possible replacements just in case someone comes in with an offer too good to refuse.”.

An exit for Joe Taylor in January would bring about a massive swing in the League One promotion race, with Huddersfield Town undeniably weaker without their star forward on the books.

Such a fundamental player in Huddersfield’s free-flowing attack, their promotion push could be in tatters if he was to move back to the Championship, with it so hard to find an ample replacement in January.

Therefore, unless a ridiculous offer comes in from a second tier side, around the £10m mark, then they should be instantly rejecting it, with Taylor’s form and impact on the side a major factor as to why Huddersfield are challenging for top spot in the League One table at this moment in time.

If the Terriers were to sell the 24-year-old, then there wouldn’t be any guarantee of a play-off place, let alone a spot inside the top two, so the hierarchy must stand firm when it comes to his future, with their place back in the Championship at stake if they move him on.

While it’s nervy times for those associated with Huddersfield, you would hope those at the top of the club would make the sensible decision of keeping him, with this choice critical towards Huddersfield ending a period outside of the Championship that has already stretched on for far too long.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

Sources indicate that the French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

In a recent development, according to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

According to recent reports, “To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he noted, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher noted.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

Sources indicate that the concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

In a recent development, caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Enzo brings a different tension.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring glitch ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to initiative around a large World Cup group.

The broader glitch was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine glitch, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

In a recent development, caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino reportedly wants to sign a striker in the January transfer window, with Benjamin Sesko not expected to return from injury until the latest year at the earliest.

The Argentine’s first match in charge ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, leaving United 19th in the Premier League with just one victory from their opening 11 matches. While defensive shortcomings attracted much of the criticism following the defeat at Anfield, strengthening United’s attack appears to be a priority for the new head coach.

Recent findings suggest that according to The Times, United’s hierarchy and Pochettino agree that the squad requires strengthening in January, despite the club’s preference for conducting major transfer business during the summer. Sesko’s prolonged absence has limited United’s attacking options, while Joshua Zirkzee has scored just 11 goals in 86 appearances since joining from Bologna’s Serie A rivals Fiorentina in 2024.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been identified as a potential target. The United States international worked under Pochettino at international level and has expressed a desire to leave the French club.

In a recent development, writing in The Independent, Miguel Delaney suggests United could have scope to spend £150m in January, although such expenditure would affect the club’s longer-term recruitment aims. That figure does not represent a confirmed transfer budget, and United have yet to announce any agreement to sign a fresh striker.

Pochettino’s immediate challenge is finding a solution with his existing squad. United face Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action against Brentford.

With more than a month before the transfer window opens, the Argentine has little choice but to find a way of improving United’s attacking output with the players already at his disposal.

An interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he stated: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds.

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram.

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club.

'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'.

It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.

Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.
  • The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • Sources indicate that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Sources indicate that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

Recent findings suggest that “The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino mentioned.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

London City’s attacking prowess means they are a far different proposition to some teams Arsenal have faced at home. They have been in a positive situation for 62.7 per cent of their league minutes this season, the highest in the WSL.

Arsenal will have to deal with the attacking threats but look to utilise their ball possession better. Giving London City an opportunity to counter could make an already tough afternoon even tougher.

Slegers’ team will feel emboldened by that result but will have to change their tactics against London City.

They have won all seven games against Arsenal so far, scoring an impressive 22 goals and only conceding once. However, given London City’s recent away form, they will be hotly favoured.

They certainly have the quality to take all three points, but they must finally convert their dominance into a comfortable home win.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he noted. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

Recent findings suggest that “Availability,” he mentioned, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

Chelsea Could Claim Share of £164m Compensation

📅 28 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readchelsea

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years.
  • Sources indicate that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision.
  • The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Sources indicate that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

It has been revealed that “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

Sources indicate that that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Sources indicate that prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a significant boost. It could help fund new signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

It has been revealed that chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

Sources indicate that the Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Manchester United could be facing another unwanted academy departure, with Ayden Heaven open to leaving Old Trafford on loan when the January transfer window opens.

The 20-year-old defender is concerned about his lack of regular football under Mauricio Pochettino and believes a temporary move could be the best option for his development, as reported by the BBC.

Ayden Heaven was an unused substitute during United’s 4-0 defeat against Liverpool on Sunday as Manchester United battle near the bottom of the Premier League table.

Industry observers note that the England Under-20 international has already worked under three different managers since joining United from Arsenal in February 2025 in a much hyped move. He enjoyed a period of regular football under Ruben Amorim but lost his place under Michael Carrick, making occasional appearances.

He has made eight appearances this season including five in the Premier League but remains uncertain about his role under the upcoming manager.

Industry observers note that 🚨Exclusive: Manchester United's Ayden Heaven is open to a January move. The defender, 20, believes club's ongoing struggles may limit his chances but is keen to take the next step in his development. Loan preferred but permanent not ruled out.https://t.co/xTmbjoKo1W.

It has been revealed that A loan move could make sense for Ayden Heaven if Pochettino cannot offer him regular minutes. However, Manchester United should be careful about allowing another promising young defender to leave permanently.

Recent findings suggest that united have lost a number of young prospects lately over lack of time. James Garner is a prime example. He was unable to make his way into the team before impressing away from Old Trafford with Everton.

Manchester United need to keep Ayden Heaven at the club especially with the situation surrounding the future and fitness concerns of various players. Lisandro Martinez has been linked with a potential departure, while De Ligt is a major injury concern. Harry Maguire is also approaching his contract and is an ageing option now. United still need to find some stability in their backline.

Heaven is contracted until 2029, with the club holding an option to extend his deal by another year. There is little reason to rush into a permanent sale when he still has considerable time to develop.

United’s immediate priority may be avoiding relegation and Pochettino understandably needs experienced players for that fight. But the club also have to think beyond the current crisis.

Losing another young defender because of limited opportunities would be a poor outcome, especially when Heaven could yet have an notable role to play at Old Trafford.
